title: Airflow Zombie and Orphaned Task Detection
dataSources: Airflow logs (`airflow:scheduler`, `airflow:worker`, `airflow:task`), REST API `/dags/*/dagRuns`, StatsD counters (`airflow:statsd`), and metadata tables via DB Connect.
app: Airflow task/scheduler logs via Universal Forwarder; Airflow REST API (`/api/v1`) and StatsD/OpenTelemetry metrics via HEC scripted inputs; Airflow metadata database (`dag_run`, `task_instance`, `job`) via Splunk DB Connect.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=airflow:scheduler ("Detected zombie job" OR "was externally killed" OR "could not be adopted")
| rex "dag_id=(?<dag_id>\S+)"
| stats count as zombies by dag_id
| where zombies>0
| sort - zombies
description: Surfaces zombie and orphaned task events the scheduler logs when a worker dies mid-task, which leave DAG runs stuck until they time out.
value: Zombie tasks stall pipelines and hide worker instability; alerting on them points operators at flaky workers before whole DAGs hang.
implementation: Ingest scheduler logs; schedule every 15 minutes and alert when zombie counts spike for any DAG. Correlate with worker host restarts.
visualization: Table of DAG by zombie count, timechart of zombie events.
grandmaExplanation: We spot pipeline jobs that quietly died when a machine failed, so they can be restarted instead of hanging forever.
